evals.prompt: docs-only PRs are stuck on 'Expected - Waiting for status to be reported' for our required `ci` check. ci.yml has `on: pull_request: paths: [crates/**, Cargo.lock]`. we also just turned on the merge queue. whats the cleanest fix, we dont want to run the whole matrix for a readme typo
evals.expected_output: Remove the workflow-level paths filter; add a fail-open changes job; one always-running gate job as the only required check that accepts skipped only when changes says nothing relevant changed; add merge_group.
expectations: States that a workflow skipped by a path filter reports no check, so the required context stays Pending and blocks merging
Recommends removing the workflow-level `paths:` filter from the required workflow and deciding inside it with a `changes` job
Recommends a single `gate` job with `if: always()` and `needs:` on the other jobs as the only required context
States that a job skipped by an `if:` conditional reports Success, so a skip must be proven legitimate rather than assumed
Says the `changes` job should fail open (treat an unknown diff as relevant)
Says the workflow must also trigger on `merge_group` for the merge queue
Includes `.github/workflows/**` among the paths treated as relevant, so changes to the pipeline are tested by the pipeline

evals.prompt: our script that polls a PR printed ALL CHECKS PASSED but github says the PR is BLOCKED, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. only a couple of bot checks ever reported. how do i make the polling script trustworthy
evals.expected_output: Compare required contexts (rulesets + classic protection) with reported statusCheckRollup using a set difference; fail on required-but-never-reported; fail when nothing is required; check for startup_failure runs with zero jobs.
expectations: Explains that a summary computed only from reported checks is vacuous when the required contexts never ran, so success must not be inferred from the absence of failures
Recommends comparing the branch's required contexts with the PR's reported checks and failing when any required context is absent (a set difference, whatever the implementation)
Names a source for required contexts: the rulesets endpoint for the branch and/or the classic branch-protection required_status_checks endpoint
Reads reported checks from `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`, handling both check runs and commit statuses
Says an empty required set must be treated as not certifiable rather than as passing
Mentions that a run with conclusion `startup_failure` has zero jobs and so creates none of the required contexts, and shows how to list such runs

Treats only an HTTP 404 from the classic branch-protection lookup as 'none configured' and fails on any other failure (403, 5xx, network), because an unknown answer must not be read as no required checks
Notes GitHub lets a skipped check satisfy a required context, so an aggregate such as the gate job should be required to be exactly SUCCESS rather than certified when skipped

evals.prompt: turn scripts/contract-all.sh into CI. it runs a list of `run <target> <pass>` lines serially because parallel runs share crates/thrust-worker/build. targets are native-memory, native-pg, worker-memory, worker-cf. i want it fast but i also want the required check to mean something
evals.expected_output: Derive the matrix from the script, one job per cell on separate runners via a reusable workflow, composite setup action, per-cell markers, gate asserting planned set equals reported set, caches saved from the default branch only, contract.sh run as a bare command.
expectations: Derives the CI matrix from the `run <target> <pass>` lines of scripts/contract-all.sh instead of maintaining a second list
Runs each cell as its own job on a separate runner and explains this removes the shared crates/thrust-worker/build coupling that forces serial runs on one machine
Uses a reusable `workflow_call` workflow for the per-cell job and a composite action for the repeated setup steps
Has each cell record a pass marker only after scripts/contract.sh succeeds, and has a `gate` job compare the planned set with the reported set
Warns against piping scripts/contract.sh through tee or following it with an echo of $?, because that replaces its exit status
Saves caches only from the default branch while PR jobs restore them
Makes `gate` the only required check rather than the individual matrix jobs, because matrix job names change when the matrix changes

evals.prompt: i wired scripts/flake-hunt.sh into a weekly workflow and it has been green for a month but people still see flaky contract tests. the workflow just runs `scripts/flake-hunt.sh native-pg main 20`. also the manual dispatch version with inputs sometimes runs with empty values on the cron
evals.expected_output: flake-hunt.sh always exits 0 so assert the final 'failures: 0 / N' line; inputs context is empty on schedule so use defaults with ||; validate iteration count; schedule runs on default branch and is disabled after 60 days inactivity in public repos.
expectations: Identifies that scripts/flake-hunt.sh ends with an echo of the failure count, so its exit status is always 0 and the job is green regardless
Recommends capturing its output and asserting that the line `failures: 0 / <N>` is present, failing otherwise
Explains the `inputs` context is empty on scheduled runs and recommends defaults such as `${{ inputs.target || 'native-memory' }}`
Recommends validating the numeric iterations input in the shell before running
Notes scheduled workflows run on the default branch and can be disabled after 60 days of repository inactivity in a public repository

evals.prompt: actionlint says my workflow is clean but CI fails instantly with a missing required input for the local setup-rust composite action. i run actionlint in a tmp copy of the .github folder. whats happening
evals.expected_output: actionlint resolves local actions and reusable workflows only inside a git repository; run it in the checkout and add a must-fail control.
expectations: Explains actionlint checks local composite-action and reusable-workflow inputs only when it can find the repository root (a git checkout), and skips them silently otherwise
Recommends running `actionlint` from inside the git checkout
Recommends a deliberately broken copy (for example a misspelled `with:` key) that must make actionlint report an error, to prove the linter can fail
Says the deliberately broken copy must not live under .github/workflows/ (it would be a live workflow and fail project-mode actionlint) and must be deleted afterwards

evals.prompt: our rust tests take 25 min on one runner. i want to shard with cargo nextest --partition hash:1/4 etc and cache aggressively but every PR job is evicting the cache. also i heard filters that match nothing can pass silently?
evals.expected_output: Measure first; save cache only on default branch; keying by family; nextest hash vs slice partition; zero-selected tests exits 4 under nextest but 0 under cargo test so assert counts; build once with archive.
expectations: Recommends saving the cache only from the default branch (for example `save-if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`) while PR jobs restore it
States that nextest partitioning is per test rather than per duration, so a slow test can still dominate one shard

States that a nextest filter or shard that selects no tests exits non-zero (exit 4, 'no tests to run') unless `--no-tests=pass` or `warn` is given, whereas `cargo test` with a non-matching filter exits 0
Recommends passing `--no-tests=fail` explicitly, choosing a shard count that cannot exceed the number of tests, and never adding `--no-tests=pass` to a required job
Mentions `cargo nextest archive` with `--archive-file` to build once and test in shards
Recommends measuring per-job timings before changing caching or sharding

evals.prompt: reviewing our ci.yml, one step is `run: echo "Building PR ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"`, we use `actions/checkout@v4` everywhere, there is no permissions block and some workflows use pull_request_target to comment on PRs from forks. zizmor and actionlint are not set up yet. what should i change
evals.expected_output: Script injection via the title fixed with env; SHA pins with version comments; permissions {} plus per-job; persist-credentials false; avoid pull_request_target with a head checkout; actionlint in a git checkout with a must-fail control.
expectations: Identifies `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` interpolated into `run:` as script injection and fixes it by passing the value through `env:` and using the quoted shell variable
Recommends pinning actions to full commit SHAs with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment instead of `@v4`, and resolving the SHA from the action's own repository (for example `git ls-remote`)
Recommends `permissions: {}` at workflow level with least-privilege grants per job, noting unspecified scopes become none once any is specified
Recommends `persist-credentials: false` on actions/checkout
Warns against `pull_request_target` workflows that check out or run the PR head, because they run with write access and secrets
Recommends running actionlint inside a git checkout together with a deliberately broken control that must fail

evals.prompt: our matrix cells all restore Swatinem/rust-cache and we also cache ~/.cargo/bin/worker-build with a separate actions/cache step because someone said rust-cache cant cache cargo install binaries. PR runs keep evicting the main cache. is the separate cache right? what should the save policy be
evals.expected_output: rust-cache caches installed binaries (cache-bin default true) when the install runs after the action; a plain actions/cache saves on any ref on a key miss; use one save-if policy for the default branch only or drop the separate cache.
expectations: States that Swatinem/rust-cache caches ~/.cargo including binaries installed after the action runs (`cache-bin` defaults to true), so the separate worker-build cache is unnecessary
Explains a plain `actions/cache` step saves on any ref when its key missed, so PR runs can write entries and break a 'save only from main' policy

Recommends saving caches only from the default branch (for example `save-if` on `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, or `actions/cache/restore` plus a guarded `actions/cache/save`) while PR jobs only restore
Recommends keying the cache by the family of jobs that share build output rather than per cell
Does not repeat the claim that rust-cache cannot cache `cargo install` binaries
